summary: Implemented and gated E-FAST-M6 (EX-20260823-fast-m6-reveal-sampling-port-be23e203): ported the native factored reveal-sampling chance node (N disc strata x M reveal samples, scenario s = r*N + d over T = N*M, disc-major enumeration) into the fast memo engine as drop7::fastr::FastFactoredSearch, with the M=1 path kept verbatim behind an M==1 branch and the one-entry leaf memo retained under M>1 (board-memcmp keying cannot alias across reveal samples; memo sits below the work increment). Built the equivalence gate against the genuine native source (machine-checked no-entry copy, thread_local diagnostics only) and executed the frozen gates: 6,300 grid decisions over d3/d4 x N5/N7 x M1/M2/M6 with 0 column/work/completed-depth mismatches; 3 retained C0 games replayed by the fast engine to byte-for-value final identity (335 decisions, 0 mismatches); 2,100-decision M=1 bit-identity regression; thread/run determinism, memo-on/off identity and mirror invariance (one disclosed harness iteration: symmetric-board mirror exclusion per finding-13 4C); 8 CRN continuations byte-identical. Realised speedup 4.4-5.9x (play duty 5.56x, continuation duty 5.60x at d3 N7M6), below the 10-40x hoped for in the hypothesis and reported as measured.
